title: USB Cam Preview camera profile
description: Describes one kind of camera so USB Cam Preview can recognise it and open it with the right settings. One file per camera in public/cameras/, named <id>.json.

id.description: Kebab-case id. Must equal the file name without .json. Convention: <brand-or-kind>-<vendorId>-<productId>, e.g. endoscope-0bda-5806.

name.description: Human readable name shown in the app.

aliases.description: Other names the same camera is sold under, or the maker of the module inside it (e.g. "InfiRay"). Shown next to the name in the app so people with a rebranded camera find it.

kind.description: What the camera is. Used for defaults and wording in the app.

generic.description: true for fallback profiles that are matched by name keywords instead of a specific device. Contributors normally never add generic profiles.

match.description: How the app recognises the camera. A USB ID match always wins over a name match.

labels.description: Case-insensitive regular expressions tested against the device name (without the "(vid:pid)" suffix Chrome adds). Only add them when the name is distinctive.

fallback.description: Matches any camera. Only for the generic-uvc profile.

modes.description: Native modes the camera really delivers, measured with the compatibility test. Never copy numbers from the box.

defaultMode.description: Mode the app opens the camera with. Must be one of modes.

mirror.description: Mirror the image horizontally by default (true for selfie webcams).

overlay.description: Default overlay drawn over the image.

controls.description: Default hardware control values applied when the browser exposes them, e.g. {"sharpness": 3}. Keys are MediaTrack constraint names.

type.description: none: no photo button. keyboard: the button sends a key press. unknown: has a button the browser cannot see, or not tested.

driver.description: For camera types that need code, not just settings: the driver (a folder in public/drivers/) that handles this camera, and its options. See public/drivers/README.md.

options.description: Driver-specific settings; each driver documents and validates its own (e.g. infiray-thermal: { "divisor": 64 }).

connection.description: How the camera has to be plugged in.

needsHub.description: true when the camera only connected through a USB hub (ideally a powered one), not plugged straight into the computer.

notes.description: What was tried, e.g. which computer and port failed and which hub worked.
Quirks worth knowing: real vs advertised resolution, LED control, cable length, etc.
